fix: Handle TOC items with uid=None to prevent TypeError when writing EPUB (#484)

Some EPUB files have TOC (Table of Contents) items where the uid attribute
is None. When ebooklib tries to write the NCX file, it passes this None
value to lxml's SubElement which expects bytes or unicode, causing a
TypeError.

This fix adds a _fix_toc_uids() method that recursively processes the TOC
and assigns auto-generated uids (navpoint-0, navpoint-1, etc.) to any
items that have uid=None.

* fix(openai): put the target language in the structured output schema

Structured Outputs pinned the shape of the answer but never the language.
`SingleTranslation.translated` and `BatchTranslation.paragraphs` were static
and description-less, so the only mention of the target language was the
`{language}` interpolated into the middle of the user prompt.

The batch path made that worse: the appended instruction was shape-only
("Return a JSON object with a 'paragraphs' array containing EXACTLY N
translated strings"), so the last thing the model read before decoding said
nothing about the language, while `{language}` sat behind a json.dumps() blob
that grows with batch size.

Derive the field name, its description and the schema name from the language
instead: "simplified chinese" -> `simplified_chinese_translation` /
`simplified_chinese_paragraphs`, described as "The source text translated into
simplified chinese. Write simplified chinese only." Models are built with
create_model behind an lru_cache, so it is one model per language rather than
one per paragraph. An empty language falls back to the previous field names.

The batch instruction now ends on the language rather than on the shape.

`_read_batch_choice` takes the language explicitly (it is a staticmethod
because results are read by a later process that never probed) and now raises
when a JSON object arrives without the expected key instead of returning the
raw payload, which would have pasted JSON into the book. A language-derived
key makes that mismatch far likelier: a batch result file cannot be resumed
under a different --language.

The capability probe stays deliberately language-free — it asks whether the
endpoint honors schemas at all, and a translation-shaped probe would confuse
that with a bad translation.

fix(md): occupy all --use_context workers regardless of heading shape (#547)

Sections for the parallel context path were keyed by top-level heading
only, so a book with a single H1 (or no headings) collapsed into one
section and ran fully sequential no matter how many --parallel-workers
were requested.

Replace the fixed H1 split with a worker-share partition:

- group batches into finest heading units (full breadcrumb); a heading
  unit is atomic so context accumulates in reading order inside it
- window breadcrumb-less runs larger than one worker share
  (total chars / workers) so heading-less documents parallelize too
- greedily coalesce contiguous units up to one share: small neighbors
  run sequentially on one translator clone with context carried across
  them, big units keep a worker to themselves
- submit sections largest-first to minimize makespan; results stay
  batch-index addressed, so output order is unchanged

Low worker counts therefore degrade toward the sequential context
quality on their own: share grows, sections coarsen, and
--parallel-workers 1 never splits at all. Resume/interrupt persistence
and per-section context isolation are untouched.

fix(epub): keep translated output valid EPUB 3 (#552)

Translating a book currently introduces validation errors the source book
did not have. Three separate causes, all in the code that writes the
output rather than the code that translates it, all reproducible on the
IDPF/W3C epub3-samples books with epubcheck 5.3.0:

1. Duplicate IDs (RSC-005). Bilingual insertion clones the source element
   with copy(p), so the clone carries the original's id and every id
   inside it. Two elements then answer to one fragment identifier, and an
   internal cross-reference may land on the translation instead of the
   passage it cites. jlreq-in-english.epub: 62 errors.

2. Restricted container content models (RSC-005). A <figure> accepts one
   <figcaption> and an EPUB 3 navigation document accepts one heading
   before its <ol> and nothing but <a>/<span> inside an <li>. A translated
   sibling there is invalid markup. The translation now joins the
   element's own content instead, so a table-of-contents entry reads
   "Chapter 1 第一章" and stays valid. For a nav <li> the translation goes
   inside the entry's <a>/<span>: the <li>'s whole content model is
   "(a | span), ol?", so appending to the <li> is as invalid as a sibling.

3. Dangling spine toc reference (OPF-049) and <link> metadata (RSC-005).
   ebooklib always writes <spine toc="ncx">, so a book whose source has no
   NCX gets a reference to a manifest item that does not exist; adding the
   item also restores the EPUB 2 fallback table of contents. Separately,
   ebooklib parses OPF <link rel=… href=…> into metadata but writes every
   metadata entry back as <meta>, where neither attribute is legal, so a
   book fails validation over an accessibility statement it merely copied.

The insertion rules live in helper.py and are applied at both places that
clone a paragraph — helper.insert_trans and the excluded-tag branch of
_insert_trans_preserving_tags — so tag mode and --plan-classify mode are
covered by one rule.

Measured on accessible_epub_3.epub (epubcheck findings, source has none):

  --translate-tags p (default)          5 -> 0
  --translate-tags p,h1,h2,h3,figcaption  104 -> 0
  --plan-classify most                244 -> 0

and across other samples in default tag mode: jlreq-in-english 62 -> 0,
figure-gallery-bindings 56 -> 1 (its source carries that one), trees
15 -> 1, wasteland 12 -> 1, moby-dick 6 -> 1, linear-algebra 5 -> 0,
internallinks 0 -> 0. The findings that remain are unrelated to these
three causes: OPF-014 manifest properties, OPF-028 undeclared metadata
prefixes, RSC-010 resource types, and duplicate id attributes inside
content.opf — all from the metadata/manifest rewrite, none addressed here.

tests/test_epub_output_validity.py covers each defect and the two ways
the rules could overreach (single-translate must keep the original's ids;
an ordinary paragraph must still get a translated sibling). 12 of its 16

`--translate-tags p` decides what to translate by tag name, and tag names

refactor(cli): choose a translator by endpoint, not by model name (#561)

--model decided three things at once: which vendor SDK to import, which
endpoint to call, and which model to name. Adding a model meant editing the
CLI, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint nobody had written a class for could
not be reached at all, even though its wire format was already implemented.

A translator is now an endpoint, described by four flags:

  --api_base    the endpoint URL; defaults to the format's official host
  --key         the credential (--api_key is the same flag)
  --model <id>  the model id exactly as that endpoint spells it
  --api_format  the API the endpoint speaks: openai, anthropic, codex,
                gemini, qwen, groq, xai, litellm, or a fixed engine

--provider NAME reads the same values from an entry in bbm_providers.json,
so a gateway is configured once; explicit flags win over the entry.

No translator is deleted. gemini and qwen keep their own classes, because
neither endpoint speaks the OpenAI shape — Gemini has its own SDK and batch
API, Qwen-MT takes source and target language as request fields rather than
as a prompt. groq, xai and litellm differed from the OpenAI class only by a

session context, batching, the model check, the usage meter. Their SDK
dependencies do not come back: those endpoints are called over the OpenAI
request path.

Two independent lines of work on the current endpoint surface (post-#561).

- **Refuse DRM.** An encrypted (Adobe/Kobo-DRM) EPUB is declined with a clear

- **Say what made it.** The output carries rights/disclosure metadata — the
  tool as a translator contributor and a two-line `dc:description`, `AI
  translation (<model>, <year>)` on the model routes or `Machine
  translation (<engine>, <year>)` on the engine formats, then the caveat —
  and an in-book translation note; the note is reflowable even inside a
  fixed-layout spine. `--no_disclosure` leaves all of it out. Package prefixes

  first.

  the OpenAI request path (`openai`, and so `groq`/`xai`/`litellm`/`--model
  orcarouter`) and the `anthropic` route. They are carried on **every** request
  the run makes, including the capability probe, the model check and the model
  listing, so the endpoint is graded on the shape the run actually sends.

  say so and continue rather than printing success and dropping the fields.

    agent-plan handoff's copyable rerun command.
- **Provider example fallback.** `bbm_providers.example.json` is a
  lowest-precedence layer, so `--provider gemini` works before the user copies
  the file — with a warning that names the shipped address and key variable,
  and with `FILL-ME` placeholder entries excluded. A real `bbm_providers.json`

Group consecutive translation units into shared requests under a
token budget instead of one request per paragraph: on the 45-book
epub-samples corpus this cuts 45k requests to under 8.7k on a
schema-verified endpoint (21k below strict decoding). Plan mode now
runs on any conversational endpoint - schema-verified routes get
structured replies, everything else a plain conversation - and only
engine routes (google/deepl/...) keep the p-tag-only legacy path.

The main pieces:

- Inline markers: nested inline tags become numbered placeholder
  tokens the model must echo, so mixed-markup paragraphs translate as
  one unit and the markup is restored around the reply. A reconcile
  gate scrubs marker-shaped tokens that land in visible text.
- Batch alignment guards: a miscounted reply goes down a halving
  ladder; a shifted reply is caught by wrong-slot marker evidence, and
  a count-compensated shift (merged lines padded back with a filler
  item) by numeric evidence - a digit run that leaves its own slot and
  surfaces next door, twice in the same direction, rejects the batch.
- Glossary: --glossary pins term renderings per request (terms ride
  only with the text that contains them); --glossary-auto keeps the
  renderings a session's handoff establishes. Pinned glossaries join
  the resume fingerprint and are embedded in the output with their
  sha256.
- Translation metadata: a small bbm_translation_metadata.json carrying
  the model, the date and the glossary checksum - nothing about who
  ran the tool - plus one visible line on the title page ("Translated
  by gpt-5.6-luna, 2026."). --no_disclosure removes both; reruns
  replace rather than accumulate the record.
- Measured defaults: the derived request budget is 2400-3200 tokens
  (half the largest budget measured fault-free at the 32-unit cap,
  weak models included; halved below strict decoding), the unit cap 32
  (half the measured fault-emergence level), the session compaction
  budget pinned at 8000. The eval doc in docs/session_grouping_eval.md
  carries the measurements and the per-endpoint tuning guide.
- Flag compatibility is validated at parse time with a declarative
  rule table (warn or refuse, each row demonstrated by a test);
  --plan-dry-run previews the partition, budget and route divergences
  without spending a token.
- Resume fingerprints cover the resolved prompt, model list and pinned
  glossary, so a resume under different flags is refused instead of

Prompt revise: three-section --prompt, patient retries, leaner deps and conservative grouping defaults (#565)

## 1. Custom prompt revise

`--prompt` now reads **three plain-text sections** on every LLM route:

- `user` — the per-request template (must keep `{text}`; `{language}` and `{crlf}` optional; any other `{placeholder}` is refused at parse time, before anything is paid).
- `system` — the standing system message. `--prompt`'s system now outranks the `OPENAI_API_SYS_MSG` env var (still read as a deprecated fallback).
- `style` — a standing register/tone instruction, said **once where a window starts** (system message on API routes, thread instructions on codex), never repeated per request. A user-written style also replaces the model's own style notes in session handoff reports.

A section without a native slot on a route folds into the neighbouring channel instead of being dropped, and the run prints where each section landed — so one prompt file works on any route.

Supporting changes:

- **`.md` prompt files are parsed natively.** The [PromptDown](https://github.com/btfranklin/promptdown) block form is kept (attribution retained), but the reader is now in-repo (`book_maker/prompt_file.py`), so the `promptdown` package and its console script are removed from the dependencies.
- **One shipped example** — `prompt_template.json`, carrying all three sections with `style` left empty — replaces the three per-situation sample JSONs.
- The structure contract ("Keep the paragraph structure and any inline markup exactly as it is given.") moved out of example text into a conditional, non-overridable preamble: appended only when a request's payload actually carries structure (batched bodies, multi-paragraph text, markers, unambiguous inline markup), never on a plain single paragraph, and never announced.
- **srt books merge `--prompt` on top of the loader's own prompt** section by section instead of silently discarding it (with a warning about the block-number/timeline contract when the `user` template is replaced).

## 2. Retries and dependencies

- **`backoff` → `tenacity`** (backoff was archived upstream in 2022; tenacity was already a dependency). The retry on the translate path is now *patient by design*: many users run flaky providers where a 429 or first token can be minutes away, so there is **no attempt cap** — waits grow exponentially to a 300 s ceiling and stay there, with a warning line per retry so a long tolerance never looks like a hang. It gives up **immediately** on errors waiting cannot fix: auth failures, invalid requests, missing models, `TypeError`, `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit`.
- The retry also now calls each route's `translate()` with the arguments it actually takes (the fixed MT engines are text-only; handing them a second positional was a per-paragraph `TypeError`).
- **PyDeepLX is vendored** (`book_maker/vendor/deeplx.py`) and the PyPI dependency dropped; a connect/read timeout is added so a stuck endpoint cannot hang a run.

## 3. Conservative grouping defaults, and a codebase cleanup

- Plan-mode grouping defaults are now deliberate safety margins rather than measured edges: `--max-batch-units` 32 → **16** (8 on endpoints that verify JSON mode but not a strict schema), the derived `--accumulated_num` band 2400–3200 → **1200–1600** (sub-strict floor 800), and the session compact default 8000 → **8192**. A fault-emergence eval only measured two models; a shifted slot is a wrong book, while a bigger bill is just a bigger bill. Anyone who trusts their model raises the flags explicitly — the constants' comments and `docs/session_grouping_eval.md` §7 spell out what is measured and how to adjust in each direction.
- A behavior-preserving simplification pass (−356 LOC): dead code removed, duplicated persistence/session logic lifted onto the base classes, repeated extraction passes collapsed. `--help`, the dry-run plan output and the produced epubs are byte-identical (modulo timestamps).
- README / README-CN slimmed to match: flag bullets say what a flag is and when to change it; the numbers and eval detail live in the eval doc. The doc-coverage test now exempts flags whose help says "deprecated" — they warn and point at their replacement at runtime.

## Verification

- Full suite green (2121 passed), `black` clean.
- Adversarially reviewed in three scoped passes (all findings fixed and re-verified).
- Smoke-tested end to end on real endpoints: openai (with schema, and behind schema-stripping/schema-rejecting proxies to exercise the fallback rungs), anthropic, google, codex, with and without `--use_context session`, plus prompt-file runs with a wire capture proving style lands once per window and survives compaction handoffs. Every produced epub was read back: ids and internal links intact, translations adjacent to sources with matching tag+class, zero delimiter/JSON residue.

fix(session): bound the handoff seed, snapshot the handoff file, restore on resume (#570)


Fixes the session-mode compaction death loop reported in #569 — credit
to @wzvideni for the diagnosis (`Co-authored-by` on the seed-bounding
commit). This takes the fix one level deeper than #569's accounting
change; the reasoning is laid out in a comment there.

## The bug

The handoff seed (the previous window's compact report) grew without
bound: the summary was re-summarized on top of itself and the learned
glossary rode along cumulatively, while `<book>_handoff.md` appended a
new copy every window. Once the seed alone reached
`--context-compact-at`, every paragraph triggered a paid compaction —
measured live: at a 1000-token budget the seed passed the whole budget
by window 10. A long book could grow the file toward #569's 50MB
report, with the report *completions* alone costing on the order of
$100+.

## The fix: bound the seed, don't re-account it

`--context-compact-at` keeps bounding the **total** window (operators
use it to target a model's max input). Instead the seed itself is
bounded, three layers deep:

1. the compact prompt asks for a ~300-token report (a shown markdown
   template — `## Summary` / `## Style` / `## Renderings` — sized to
   what models naturally write, measured mean 246 / p95 373);
2. `max_tokens=500` on the compact request where the endpoint accepts
   it (with reasoning-token allowance on the `max_completion_tokens`
   spelling);
3. an unconditional client-side truncation at 512 tokens, head-first
   at a line boundary.

512 < 1500 (the raised minimum budget), so a window always has room
for translation content: the loop is arithmetically impossible.

The model's reply never has to be well-formed for this to hold.
Whatever comes back, glossary lines are grepped out (`→`/`->`), the
rest is trimmed of headings/tags/labels and truncated to the cap, and
that seeds the next window. There is no retry ladder on format — only
transport errors or an empty reply take the failed-compact path (which
defers and retries on the next unit, up to 3 times).

## Handoff file: append log → snapshot

`<book>_handoff.md` is now a small versioned snapshot, atomically
overwritten (`tmp` + `os.replace`) each compaction: current summary,
style note, and the merged glossary with replace-not-append semantics.
It stays 1.6–3.4KB regardless of book length — it tracks terms, not
windows. Old append-log files are detected and ignored with a warning.

## Glossary hardening (from testing cheap models on the compact turn)

- New/changed terms only, capped at 16 per report; the accumulated set
  is deduped client-side (changed renderings replace, pinned terms
  win).
- Reversed pairs (`translation → term`) are detected and flipped, not
  dropped; identity and multi-alternative hedges are dropped.
- A harvested pair must be *grounded*: one end has to actually occur
  in the window's sources or translations.
- `--glossary-auto` now defaults **off** — reporting your own
  renderings accurately takes a capable model. Enable it explicitly.

## Style

A style the operator fixes via `--prompt` stands untouched, always.
When none is fixed, the style the model reports at each compaction
becomes the standing style instruction for the next window (newest
replaces previous; a report without one leaves it alone), so observed
register survives window seams without riding the seed.

## Resume

`--resume` on a session run now restores the snapshot: the summary
seeds the fresh window, the standing style note comes back, and (when
`--glossary-auto` is on) learned terms are restored, pinned terms on
top. Gated so a stale handoff file can never switch glossary behavior
on for runs that didn't ask.

## Floor: `--context-compact-at` minimum is 1500

Measured (60-unit book, matched runs): total session cost is **flat**
in the budget — there is no cost cliff at any setting. What a small
budget does cost is continuity: request grouping packs ~1200 source
tokens per request, so below ~2400 every window holds roughly one
request and compaction saturates at once-per-request (8–9 compactions
at every budget ≤2000, vs 4 at 3000, 2 at 8192) — consecutive
requests share only the ~150-token summary while every handoff report
is still paid for. Below 1500, session mode adds cost and seams
without adding context; use window mode (`--use_context`) instead,
and the rejection message says so.

The redesign also cut absolute cost at every measured budget (the
cumulative glossary riding the seed was the dominant hidden cost):

| budget | before | after | saving |
|-------:|-------:|------:|-------:|
| 1000 | $0.291 | $0.227 | −21.9% |
| 1500 | $0.261 | $0.223 | −14.7% |
| 2000 | $0.266 | $0.232 | −12.8% |
| 3000 | $0.250 | $0.236 | −5.6% |

feat(pdf): --to-epub, a bilingual reflowable EPUB with navigation from a PDF (#574)


### What this adds

```bash
pip install ".[pdf]"          # from a checkout; brings docling and PyTorch
make_book.py --book_name paper.pdf --to-epub --use_context session
```

That reads the PDF, translates it, and writes a **bilingual, reflowable
EPUB with a table of contents** beside it as `paper_bilingual.epub`: every
paragraph followed by its translation, the paper's headings as the EPUB
navigation, figures and display formulas as pictures, tables as tables.

A PDF without `--to-epub` still takes the existing text loader, unchanged
(and #571's glossary and session support for it applies there). This PR
adds a separate route beside it, in three stages, each resumable:

1. **Extraction** with [docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling)
   (layout and table models, CPU or GPU). The PDF's own text layer is used;
   OCR is opt-in (`--pdf-ocr`) and then runs only on pages that have no
   text layer. A scanned page without the flag is refused before anything
   is paid for, never silently skipped. The result is `source.md` plus
   images in a bundle `<name>_book/` that can be read and edited before a
   model is called.
2. **Translation** through the existing Markdown loader via a small
   reading-edition subclass that pairs each block with its translation and
   keeps the original headings structural. Every Markdown-loader flag
   works the same here (`--use_context session`, `--glossary`,
   `--parallel-workers`, `--test`, `--prompt`, …); parity is pinned by
   tests. A rerun reuses the extraction and a finished translation.
3. **Export** with Pandoc; the navigation follows the headings, and an
   EPUB whose contents do not point at headings is refused rather than
   shipped.

### What changed since the first version of this PR

Reviewers who read the September 21 body: the route no longer uses
OpenDataLoader's Java engine. A JRE is a system install that Python
packaging cannot express, and the time it saved over docling was under
three seconds on a five-page cut, so docling is the only parser and the
whole route is one optional extra. Since then the branch gained, each
measured before it was kept:

- **Hidden-text figures** (`pdf_sanitize.py`): a vector figure can carry
  its content a hundred times under small clip windows and every
  extractor reads all of it (the first arXiv paper came out as a
  2,246-page EPUB). Such figures are rasterized in a working copy before
  extraction; on 75 arXiv papers it fired six times, on genuine figures
  only, never on visible text.
- **Heading levels from the page** (`pdf_headings.py`): docling writes
  every heading as `##`; numbering decides first, then the glyph size and
  weight under the heading box. 95.9% exact levels on 20 arXiv papers;
  docling's own optional hierarchy model measured 24.6% on the same set,
  so it stays off.
- **Display formulas as pictures** (`pdf_formula.py`): docling finds a
  formula region and never reads it; each is cropped from the page and
  placed by identity where the equation stood. `--no-formula-images`
  restores the placeholders. docling's formula enrichment stays off (it
  hallucinated and cost 29× in the eval). Inline maths is not covered.
- **JBIG2-masked scans** (`pdf_render.py`): docling-parse 7.20 ignores a
  JBIG2 `/SMask`, so Internet Archive / ABBYY scans render black and OCR
  reads nothing. Such documents get their page images from pypdfium2,
  docling-parse for everything else. Chinese scan character error rate
  0.249 → 0.010.
- **Region roles corrected by a vision model** (`--img-model`, opt-in,
  never the run's model by fallback): the page image with docling's boxes
  is shown to the model, which relabels text / heading / caption /
  footnote / code under a strict per-id schema; accepted answers are
  applied as typed replacements before export. About 3k prompt tokens per
  page.
- **`--pages`, `--ocr-lang`, `--ocr-engine`, `--ocr-replace-layer`,
  `--device`**: read a page range into its own bundle; name the OCR
  languages (engine codes or `iso:` tags; a scan in another script says so
  when the flag is missing); choose the OCR engine (rapidocr, ocrmac,
  easyocr, tesseract; a missing one is refused with its install line;
  measured on 13 scans: ocrmac and tesseract lead on English, rapidocr on
  simplified Chinese, ocrmac downloads nothing on a Mac); replace a garbage
  text layer with OCR on every page; choose the processor (`auto` finds
  CUDA or MPS and falls back to CPU, which gives the same output, slower).
- **Extraction settings are one value** (`pdf_settings.py`): the manifest
  records what docling was configured with, and a rerun that changes any
  of it extracts again; device and docling version are provenance only.
- **Sidecar endpoints** (`endpoints.py`): `--img-model/--img-base-url/
  --img-key` for the role pass and `--classify-model/--classify-base-url/
  --classify-key` for plan mode's classifier (an EPUB feature already on
  `main`; this is the endpoint split). A key is bound to the address it
  was given for and never travels to another host. `--classify-model jev`
  reaches TypeSafe's Jev classifier and Jev-compatible servers;
  `--classify-min-confidence` (default 0.95, measured over 662 signatures
  on 45 EPUBs) turns a low-confidence skip back into a translate.
- **`--no-thinking`** negotiates the endpoint's reasoning field; every
  compatibility *stop* row is applied before extraction, so a bad flag
  combination is refused before anything is paid for.
- **The translation identity is what was typed**: the bundle's translation
  fingerprint records only non-default options, so adding a flag no longer
  invalidates finished bundles.
